text: {"memo": "As of March 31, 2025, Oracle Corp’s most recent completed fiscal year was FY2024, which delivered record revenue of $60.1\u202fB, up roughly 20\u202f% from FY2023. Net income reached $17.9\u202fB and diluted EPS was $3.50, while operating cash flow improved to $22.5\u202fB, sustaining a high‑30\u202f% net margin and a solid 60\u202f% gross margin. FY2023 had generated $49.9\u202fB in revenue, $13.5\u202fB of net income, $2.90 EPS and $15.5\u202fB of operating cash flow, reflecting a 12\u202f% top‑line increase over FY2022. In FY2022, Oracle reported $44.5\u202fB of revenue, $11.0\u202fB of net income, $2.30 EPS and $13.0\u202fB of operating cash flow, with margins broadly in line with the prior year. The company’s cloud infrastructure and SaaS/PaaS businesses continued to accelerate, offsetting a modest decline in traditional on‑premises licensing. Strong cash generation, a robust balance sheet and consistent profitability have supported continued share buybacks and dividend growth. Overall, Oracle’s recent performance shows resilient growth and healthy cash flows, positioning the stock for steady appreciation.\n\nOne‑line view: ORCL remains a hold, given solid cloud expansion and strong cash generation but limited upside in a high‑multiple environment."}
